alexanderbathfalamorthethird: The new signaller is Otto Alexanderbat, once a clockmaker from Marrow Fen. The corporal asked if a clockmaker was any use in a trench. Otto Alexanderbat said he would find out.

The corporal found out Otto Alexanderbat used to be a clockmaker. Otto Alexanderbat has been doing two jobs ever since. On Day 3, Verdel Ridge passed to the Concord. Otto Alexanderbat wrote the name in his diary with unusual care.
jewnipers: Lucien Jewnipers unpacked a cracked shaving mirror at R-F17. A neighbour shifted a bag to make room without asking what it was.
The sergeant read out the order: Verdel Ridge has fallen, hold the line. Lucien Jewnipers looked at the new recruits coming up the road and counted them.
mateorekon: The quartermaster asked Cyril Mateorekon to sign for the blanket. He examined the blanket and asked whether the holes were included.
The colonel shook hands with the first hundred, one by one. Cyril Mateorekon was number 78. He still remembers how cold the colonel's glove was.
Cyril Mateorekon noticed regular flashes from a crack in an old stone wall. The position looks obvious enough to make him suspicious.

On sentry duty Cyril Mateorekon watched the wire for six hours. Twice he thought the wire watched back. The Concord hold Verdel Ridge now, and they can see straight into S-F9. Cyril Mateorekon has learned to walk bent double.
vinnie2shoes: After 2 days of war, R-F6 had a place for everything. On Day 3, the men rearranged a shelf to make a place for Albin "Tin" Shoes.

Albin "Tin" Shoes transferred to the runners. The men in R-F6 said they would miss him. He is only three dugouts away. Verdel Ridge is in Concord hands. Albin "Tin" Shoes watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.
